wine.q: Which fruit is the signature aroma of Cabernet Sauvignon?
wine.e: Blackcurrant is Cabernet Sauvignon's hallmark aroma.

wine.q: Which part of a black grape contains tannins?
wine.e: Black grape skins hold both the colour and the tannins.

wine.q: Which grape is used for white Burgundy?
wine.e: White Burgundy, including Chablis, is made from Chardonnay.

wine.q: Which group of aromas typically comes from oak?
wine.e: Oak gives vanilla, cedar, smoke, coconut and cloves.

wine.q: Why do the best wine glasses narrow at the rim?
wine.e: The shape keeps aromas in the glass so they are easier to appreciate.

wine.q: Which of these is a Spanish sparkling wine?
wine.e: Cava is the sparkling wine from Spain.

wine.q: Which herbaceous notes are typical of Sauvignon Blanc?
wine.e: Sauvignon Blanc pairs fresh fruit with asparagus, green pepper and grass.

wine.q: In a cool climate, grapes will usually have…
wine.e: The cooler it is, the more acidic and less sugary the grapes stay.

wine.q: Which grape is used for red Burgundy?
wine.e: Red Burgundy is made from Pinot Noir.

wine.q: Which structural characteristic makes your mouth water?
wine.e: Acidity makes your mouth water and gives freshness.

wine.q: How should a sparkling wine such as Champagne be served?
wine.e: Sparkling wines are served well chilled, between 6 and 10°C.

wine.q: Why is Port both sweet and high in alcohol?
o: Added alcohol stops the yeast, leaving sugar behind
It ferments for a long time in oak
wine.e: In sweet fortified wines, added alcohol kills the yeast early.

wine.q: What is Syrah called in Australia?
wine.e: Syrah in France and Shiraz in Australia are the same grape.

wine.q: Why is it possible to make white wine from black grapes?
wine.e: Colour is only in the skin; black grape juice has no colour.

wine.q: Which French wine is made from Sauvignon Blanc?
wine.e: Sancerre, a white from the Loire, is made from Sauvignon Blanc.

wine.q: Tasting a red wine, your mouth feels dry. Which characteristic are you noticing?
wine.e: Tannin, from the grape skins, dries the mouth.

wine.q: What effect does salty food have on wine?
o: It seems more bitter and acidic
It makes the alcohol stand out
wine.e: Salt makes wine less bitter and acidic, fruitier and fuller.

wine.q: Which description fits Prosecco?
o: Light Italian sparkling wine, pear and floral
Dry Spanish sparkling wine, apple and lemon
French sparkling wine with toasted bread
wine.e: Prosecco is a light Italian sparkling wine with pear and flowers.

wine.q: What range of sweetness can Riesling have?
o: Dry to sweet, always with high acidity
wine.e: Riesling can be dry, medium or sweet, but always has high acidity.

wine.q: Which is the only grape permitted in Barolo DOCG?
wine.e: Barolo DOCG is made exclusively from Nebbiolo.

spirits.q: A label reads 40% abv. What does this mean?
o: That 40% of the liquid is alcohol
That 40% of the liquid is sugar
That the spirit has been aged for 40 months
That 40% of the liquid is water
spirits.e: The abbreviation gives the percentage of alcohol in the volume of liquid.

spirits.q: Where does the smoky flavour of some Single Malts come from?
o: Peat burned while the malted barley is heated
New barrels charred on the inside
spirits.e: Peat smoke flavours the grains during the final heating of malting.

spirits.q: What is a grape brandy such as Cognac?
o: A wine strengthened with neutral spirit
A grain spirit flavoured with grapes
spirits.e: Grape juice is fermented into wine, and that wine is distilled.

spirits.q: Which flavour must lead in a gin?
spirits.e: By definition, gin must have juniper as its main flavour.

spirits.q: Where can Tequila be made?
o: Only in certain states of Mexico
spirits.e: The law limits production to certain named Mexican states.

spirits.q: What is a French 75 topped with?
spirits.e: The French 75 is a sparkling sour topped with Champagne.

spirits.q: In a pot still, which part turns the vapours back into liquid?
spirits.e: In the condenser, the vapours pass through a cooled coil and become liquid again.

spirits.q: What is a Blended Scotch whisky?
o: Malt and grain whiskies from different distilleries
Several malts from the same distillery
Grain whiskies only, of various ages
spirits.e: A blend combines both types of Scottish whisky from several distilleries.

spirits.q: What does the term VS guarantee on a Cognac?
spirits.e: VS matches the legal minimum: at least 2 years.

spirits.q: What makes a spirit a vodka?
spirits.e: Vodka is defined by its very high distillation strength.

spirits.q: Which Tequila style spends at least 12 months in oak?
spirits.e: Añejo is aged for at least 12 months and combines agave and oak.

spirits.q: What is the base spirit of a Negroni?
spirits.e: The Negroni is built on gin.

spirits.q: Compared with a used barrel, a new barrel gives a spirit...
spirits.e: A never-used barrel gives the most; each reuse weakens its effect.

spirits.q: Which grain must make up at least 51% of a Bourbon's recipe?
spirits.e: Bourbon is a corn-majority whiskey, at least 51%.

spirits.q: How must Cognac be distilled by law?
o: Once in a tall column still
Only once in a pot still
spirits.e: The law requires double distillation in a pot still.

spirits.q: What sets a liqueur apart from a plain flavoured spirit?
o: It has been aged in oak
spirits.e: Liqueur = flavoured spirit plus sugar.

spirits.q: In the Caribbean, where must rhum agricole come from?
spirits.e: In the Caribbean, rhum agricole must come from Martinique or Guadeloupe.

spirits.q: Which recipe is a Daiquiri?
spirits.e: The Daiquiri is the classic rum-based short sour.

spirits.q: What is a newly made spirit like as it leaves the still?
spirits.e: Every spirit is born clear and sugar-free; colour and sweetness only come later.

spirits.q: What is the minimum ageing for any Scotch whisky?
o: Three years, anywhere in the UK
spirits.e: All Scotch is distilled in Scotland and aged there for at least three years.

beer.q: What are the four basic ingredients of most beers?
o: Water, malted grain, hops and yeast
Malted grain, honey, yeast and salt
beer.e: Malt supplies the sugars, hops bring bitterness and aroma, and yeast turns the sugar into alcohol and bubbles.

beer.q: What is the main difference between ales and lagers?
o: The type of yeast and the fermentation temperature
Ales are always dark, lagers always pale
Ales are made only from wheat
beer.e: Ales use top-fermenting yeast at warmer temperatures; lagers use bottom-fermenting yeast at cooler temperatures. Both can be pale or dark.

beer.q: The Pilsner style is named after a town in which country?
beer.e: It was first brewed in Plzeň, in Bohemia, in 1842: a golden, crisp lager with a clear hop bitterness that was copied all over the world.

beer.q: What does the IBU scale measure in a beer?
beer.e: IBU stands for International Bitterness Units, mostly from hops. Colour has its own scales, and strength is shown as % abv.

beer.q: What do hops mainly bring to beer?
beer.e: Hop flowers balance the sweetness of the malt with bitterness and add floral, citrus or herbal aromas; they also help the beer keep.

beer.q: What is the “mash” in brewing?
o: Crushed malt soaked in hot water to release its sugars
The foam on top of the glass
beer.e: The sweet liquid drained from the mash, called wort, is then boiled with hops, cooled and fermented.

beer.q: What does IPA stand for?
beer.e: A pale ale with plenty of hops, born in England in the days of beer shipped to India; today the name stands for very hoppy, aromatic beers.

beer.q: Roughly how strong are most everyday beers?
beer.e: Some styles go much higher, such as strong Belgian ales or imperial stouts, but the beers most people drink sit around 4–6%.

beer.q: Why is barley malted before brewing?
o: So its starch can become fermentable sugar
beer.e: Soaking, sprouting and drying the grain wakes up enzymes that later turn its starch into sugars the yeast can ferment.

beer.q: What gives a stout its dark colour and roasted flavours?
o: Coffee, which every stout must contain
beer.e: Grain roasted until very dark brings the black colour and coffee or chocolate notes, even when no coffee is used at all.

beer.q: What is “dry hopping”?
o: Adding hops after the boil, for aroma rather than bitterness
Drying hops in the sun before use
Brewing a beer with no hops
Adding hops to the dry grain before mashing
beer.e: Hops added cold, during or after fermentation, give lots of fresh aroma with little extra bitterness: a hallmark of modern IPAs.

beer.q: How should beer be stored?
beer.e: Light reacts with hop compounds and gives an unpleasant “skunky” smell; brown bottles protect best.

beer.q: What mostly gives a beer its colour?
o: The malt, and how darkly it was kilned or roasted
beer.e: Pale malts give golden beers; caramel and roasted malts give amber, brown and black ones.

beer.q: What makes a beer “Trappist”?
o: It is brewed inside a Trappist monastery, under the monks' control
It is flavoured with mountain herbs
beer.e: Only a small number of abbeys around the world may use the Trappist label, and the profits must go to the community or to charity.

beer.q: Why is the wort boiled?
o: To sterilise it and draw bitterness from the hops
beer.e: The boil usually lasts 60 to 90 minutes and also helps the beer to become clear.

beer.q: Why is a head of foam welcome on most beers?
o: It holds the aromas and protects the beer from air
It shows that the beer is strong
beer.e: Clean glasses matter: grease or detergent residue makes the foam collapse.

beer.q: Which of these is the classic hop of Czech pilsners?
beer.e: Saaz is spicy and herbal. Cascade and Citra are American hops; Fuggle is English.

beer.q: Which Belgian beer ferments with wild yeasts and bacteria from the air?
beer.e: Lambic is brewed around Brussels and ferments spontaneously, giving sour, complex beers such as gueuze or cherry kriek.

beer.q: What is “bottle conditioning”?
o: A second fermentation in the bottle that creates natural fizz
Heating the bottles to kill microbes
Ageing the beer in wooden barrels
beer.e: A little sugar and live yeast go into the bottle; the fine sediment at the bottom is normal.

beer.q: What is a Märzen?
o: An amber German lager linked to Oktoberfest
A sour wheat beer from Berlin
beer.e: It was brewed in March (März) and stored cold through the summer, to be drunk in autumn.

sake.q: What is sake mainly made from?
sake.e: Sake is brewed from polished rice: the koji mould turns the rice starch into sugar, and yeast turns that sugar into alcohol.

sake.q: What does “junmai” on a sake label mean?
o: Made only from rice, koji, yeast and water, with no added distilled alcohol
sake.e: Junmai means “pure rice”. Other styles may have a small amount of distilled alcohol added to lift the aromas.

sake.q: At what temperature can sake be served?
o: Chilled, at room temperature or warm, depending on the style
sake.e: Fragrant ginjo styles are usually served cool; fuller, rice-driven styles can be lovely gently warmed.

sake.q: What is unusual about the way sake ferments?
o: Starch becomes sugar and sugar becomes alcohol at the same time, in the same tank
It ferments in oak barrels for years
It needs no yeast at all
sake.e: This “multiple parallel fermentation” lets sake reach around 18–20% alcohol naturally, before it is usually diluted with water.

sake.q: What is koji?
o: A mould grown on steamed rice that turns starch into sugar
A Korean yeast for rice wine
A quality grade on the label
sake.e: Koji does the job that malting does for beer. The same mould is used in Japan for miso and soy sauce.

sake.q: What is nigori sake?
o: Cloudy sake, coarsely filtered so some rice solids remain
sake.e: Nigori looks milky white and often tastes creamy and slightly sweet; give the bottle a gentle turn before pouring.

sake.q: What do people in Japan usually call rice sake?
sake.e: In Japanese “sake” can mean any alcoholic drink, so rice sake is often called nihonshu, “Japanese alcohol”. Shochu is a distilled spirit.

sake.q: What does the rice polishing ratio on a sake label tell you?
o: How much of each grain is left after polishing
How many years it was aged
sake.e: A ratio of 60% means 40% of every grain was polished away. The lower the number, the more polished the rice.

sake.q: For a daiginjo, the rice must be polished down to at most…
sake.e: Ginjo uses rice polished to 60% or less, daiginjo to 50% or less: these are the most refined, fragrant styles.

sake.q: About how strong is most sake as sold?
sake.e: Most sake is lightly diluted to around 15–16%. Undiluted genshu is stronger, usually 17–20%.

sake.q: What does the Sake Meter Value (nihonshu-do) roughly tell you?
o: How dry or sweet a sake is likely to taste
sake.e: The higher the positive number, the drier the sake tends to be; acidity also changes how sweet it feels, so it is only a rough guide.

sake.q: Why is rice polished before brewing sake?
o: To remove outer layers whose proteins and fats give rougher flavours
sake.e: The starchy heart of the grain gives a cleaner, more delicate and often fruitier sake.

sake.q: What is a ginjo sake typically like?
o: Light and fragrant, with fruity and floral aromas
sake.e: Highly polished rice and a slow, cool fermentation bring aromas that can recall apple, melon, pear or banana.

sake.q: What is the small cup traditionally used for drinking sake?
sake.e: The tokkuri is the flask the sake is poured from, a kura is a sake brewery, and the toji is the master brewer.

sake.q: Is sake distilled?
o: No, it is fermented (brewed), like beer and wine
sake.e: The distilled drinks of Japan are shochu and, in Okinawa, awamori.

sake.q: What does “nama” mean for a sake?
o: It is unpasteurised and must be kept in the fridge
It is meant to be served hot
sake.e: Most sake is pasteurised, usually twice. Nama sake skips this, so it tastes fresh and lively but is more fragile.

sake.q: Which is the most famous sake rice variety?
sake.e: Often called the “king of sake rice”, it is grown above all in Hyogo. Koshihikari is a table rice.

sake.q: What is honjozo?
o: Sake from rice polished to 70% or less, with a little distilled alcohol added
Sake made only from rice, with nothing added
sake.e: Honjozo is typically light, dry and easy to drink, and good served warm.

sake.q: How should an opened bottle of sake be kept?
o: In the fridge, and finished within a week or two
At room temperature for a year
sake.e: Most sake is not made for ageing: buy it fresh and store it cool and dark.

sake.q: In which season is sake traditionally brewed?
sake.e: Cold weather keeps the fermentation slow and clean; the rice harvested in autumn is brewed through the winter.
